gpui.role: Application model, entities, windows, elements, input, layout, text and scene primitives.
gpui.surface: Broad root re-exports connect private implementation modules to the application-facing API. AppContext and platform traits define important contracts.
gpui.review: Review root re-exports by subsystem. Preserve hidden macro support until generated consumers have been checked.

gpui-platform.role: Selects and constructs the native or web platform.
gpui-platform.surface: application, headless, background_executor and current_platform; additional exports depend on target and test/bench features.
gpui-platform.review: Keep platform selection separate from renderer changes. This snapshot has no iOS branch in current_platform.

gpui-apple.role: Shared Apple rendering and services, gated for macOS or iOS.
gpui-apple.surface: Metal renderer, dispatcher, optional text system, keychain and thermal modules.
gpui-apple.review: Start the Apple color investigation in metal_renderer.rs: BGRA8Unorm appears in layer and texture setup. Shared iOS code does not establish a complete iOS window backend.

gpui-macos.role: macOS windows, input, display and native platform integration.
gpui-macos.surface: MacPlatform plus a small metal_renderer export module; headless renderer depends on test/bench features.
gpui-macos.review: Trace window configuration into shared Apple rendering before proposing wide-gamut controls. Review native and headless behavior separately.

gpui-linux.role: Linux/FreeBSD platform integration with Wayland and X11 feature paths.
gpui-linux.surface: current_platform and linux_platform; implementation lives behind private modules.
gpui-linux.review: Preserve target and feature combinations when changing the shared platform contract.

gpui-windows.role: Windows native platform, Win32 windows, DirectWrite and DirectX integration.
gpui-windows.surface: WindowsPlatform is the narrow root export; most native modules are crate-private.
gpui-windows.review: A small export list still implements the shared platform contract. Check backend implementations when that contract changes.

gpui-web.role: Browser windowing, input and rendering with WebGPU and a WebGL2 fallback.
gpui-web.surface: CanvasFontFallback plus wasm-gated platform, window, dispatcher, HTTP and initialization exports.
gpui-web.review: Keep wasm exports distinct from native fallback text support. The entry documentation describes a single top-level window lifecycle restriction.

gpui-wgpu.role: GPU context, renderer, atlas and text support used across platform backends.
gpui-wgpu.surface: WgpuRenderer, WgpuContext, WgpuSurfaceConfig, atlas/text exports and a public wgpu re-export.
gpui-wgpu.review: WgpuContext exposes device and queue fields. Review the intended custom-rendering contract before narrowing these handles or adding shader extension points.

gpui-macros.role: Procedural macros for GPUI actions, elements, contexts, styling and test/benchmark support.
gpui-macros.surface: Action, IntoElement, Render, AppContext and VisualContext derives, plus procedural helper macros.
gpui-macros.review: Generated API is not expanded by this inventory. Pair macro changes with downstream compilation and inspect hidden support paths.

xgpui-shader.role: Opt-in gradients, mesh paints, portable WGSL and selectable kinetic typography.
xgpui-shader.surface: painted(), Paint, WindowPaintExt, SolidColor, Gradient, MeshGradient, portable shader producers and typography::SelectableText. Ordinary programs retain sRGB semantics; new_linear_p3 opts into native wide-SDR output.
xgpui-shader.review: Keep effects and caching in the extension; preserve the small GPUI recording/preparation contract. Wide-gamut presentation is a separate backend capability.

xgpui-gamut.role: Explicit linear-P3 SDR content producers; normal GPUI controls retain sRGB semantics.
xgpui-gamut.surface: WideColor::linear_p3 supports CustomContent; optional instanced WidePainter/WideGradient use explicit P3 shaders. Shared color math lives in xgpui-color; GPUI backends own presentation. Native color-lab compares P3 and mapped sRGB reference swatches with effective window/display status.
xgpui-gamut.review: Keep profile decoding and future content producers separate from host presentation. Windows native swap-chain/display validation remains outstanding; Linux is deferred.

xgpui-parley.role: Opt-in Parley/HarfRust text shaping, BiDi paragraphs and grayscale rasterization.
xgpui-parley.surface: ParleyTextSystem, retained face/variation identity and optional GPUI paragraph shaping/geometry. GPUI owns frame caches and the glyph atlas.
xgpui-parley.review: Preserve descriptor/resolved-face identity and immutable layouts. Explicit direction/language and Unicode conformance remain follow-ups; Windows/Linux runtime and paragraph conversion IMEs need validation.

xgpui-svg.role: Experimental full-color progressive SVG elements with optional shared raster scheduling and aggregate image accounting.
xgpui-svg.surface: SvgDocument, SvgImage/svg_image, RasterPolicy and SvgScheduler. Stable IDs retain progressive jobs; shared pools cap admitted jobs and accounted image costs. path_effects provides retained Bézier contours, cached arc lengths, normalized trim and phased dashes before native stroke tessellation.
xgpui-svg.review: Preserve stale-result rejection, atlas cleanup and reservation lifetimes. Accounting is not a hard process/GPU memory limit; viewport tiling and broader hardware validation remain follow-ups.

xgpui-color.role: Standalone CPU color science and reusable WGSL math, with zero runtime dependencies.
xgpui-color.surface: EncodedRgb, LinearRgb, RgbSpace, XyzD65, Oklab, Oklch, GamutMapping, LinearRgba, LinearGradient and WGSL_COLOR_MATH. No GPUI or GPU context required. Browser color demo reports its sRGB canvas separately from P3 display capability; a native companion displays paired sRGB/P3 samples.
xgpui-color.review: Keep conversion separate from gamut mapping and rendering. Preserve finite extended values, explicit alpha/hue rules and CPU/GPU reference tolerances.

xgpui-media.role: Large images, color adjustments and GPU-backed video previews for GPUI.
xgpui-media.surface: MediaLoader, MediaLimits, UploadLimits, FrameUploadLimits, ImageJob, MediaImage, UploadStatus and image_view. Metal/wgpu completion-driven staging reuse; shared per-scene source count/byte admission; backend-specific staging and host-only submission. ImageFilter, FilteredImage and image_view.filter provide ordered in-shader SDR RGB adjustments without reuploading source textures. VideoStream/VideoFrame provide bounded latest-frame presentation, with macOS BGRA and two-plane NV12 IOSurface import (BT.601/709, full/video range, same-pass conversion) and completion-safe snapshot lifetime; Windows dedicated immutable same-device BGRA textures have an initial native adapter (cross-checked, runtime pending); keyed NT-handle snapshots now support nonblocking ownership handoff (Windows test code cross-checks, execution pending); Linux now has an opt-in immutable linear BGRA DMA-BUF Vulkan snapshot adapter (Linux cross-check and host layout tests; GPU runtime pending). A generated Linux native fixture now exercises export/import, pixel capture, cache reuse and lifetime with Vulkan validation-error counting; the harness cross-compiles but native execution remains pending. Explicit fence import, pool reuse and foreign-family imports remain pending. A release benchmark records upload-phase versus cached render CPU samples, staging-pool reuse and pixel validation on macOS Metal/wgpu; GPU timing and zero-stutter guarantees are not claimed. The lab defaults to release builds; system playback adapters are separate follow-up work.
xgpui-media.review: Preserve completion-held exclusive buffer leases, stale-generation rejection, abandoned-recording retry and shared frame budgets. D3D11 pooling/runtime validation, chunked uploads, fairness and timing benchmarks remain pending. Limits do not bound total driver/process memory.

xgpui-canvas.role: Experimental native spatial viewport, f64 camera and retained BVH scenes.
xgpui-canvas.surface: Camera2D, PanGesture, Scene, snapping and Overview; optional GPUI Canvas and configurable GridPainter.
xgpui-canvas.review: Callers own selection and input policy. Native and browser labs cover cards and CPU fractals; rotation, isometric grids and general subtree transforms remain follow-ups.
